frostfold_arrival.speaker: patch
frostfold_arrival.text: Snow! Okay, this I can work with. Snowball fights. Sledging. A heroic fox silhouetted against a mountain.

frostfold_arrival.speaker: corrugate
frostfold_arrival.text: Fox. I'm made of cardboard. Snow is just water that's waiting.

frostfold_arrival.speaker: patch
frostfold_arrival.text: The big stitched thing holding the book together? Why's it... creaking?

frostfold_arrival.speaker: corrugate
frostfold_arrival.text: Because the Sogg's in the binding. If the spine goes, every page in this book comes loose. Us included.

frostfold_arrival.speaker: patch
frostfold_arrival.text: Right. So we climb a mountain made of book. Fine. Love that. Very normal Tuesday.

flat_arrival.speaker: patch
flat_arrival.text: Whoa. Everything's gone flat. The mountains are just... drawings on the snow.

flat_arrival.speaker: dot
flat_arrival.text: Page lies down. World lies down.

flat_arrival.speaker: corrugate
flat_arrival.text: And that cliff that had us beat is a line on the ground. Walk round it. I'll be over here, enjoying not climbing anything.

bindwell_intro.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_intro.text: Mind the stitches, dear. Oh. A fox. With a tape tail. Well, aren't you a modern sort of mend.

bindwell_intro.speaker: patch
bindwell_intro.text: Patch the Magnificent. And you're a... needle?

bindwell_intro.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_intro.text: Old Bindwell. I keep the spine sewn. Have done since the man at the table first threaded me, the year the little girl was born.

bindwell_intro.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_intro.text: The Sogg's got into the binding. The thread's going soft, and the spine's too sheer to climb without pitons. Something stiff and steel.

bindwell_intro.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_intro.text: Clever stop. Fetch me a clip from out there and I'll bend you pitons, and stand the page back up on the far side of the cliff.

bindwell_intro.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_intro.text: And if you find my spools on the way up, I dropped three of them in the wind. Bring them to me at the top and I'll pay you for your trouble.

bindwell_progress.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_progress.text: Still three spools out there, dear, frozen to the spine. And don't forget my paperclip. The page corner by me goes out onto the table.

bindwell_done.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_done.text: All three! Look at that. A bit frosty, but thread forgives you if you're patient with it.

bindwell_done.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_done.text: There. I'll restring what I can while you're up top. Take these Scraps. And fox?

bindwell_done.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_done.text: Nothing that's been stitched is ever as smooth as it was. It's stronger where the stitches are. Remember that up there.

bindwell_repeat.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_repeat.text: Off you go, dear. I'll keep the thread warm.

clip_heist_arrival.speaker: patch
clip_heist_arrival.text: Gran's table again. Later. Darker. The Great Light's buzzing like it's tired.

clip_heist_arrival.speaker: dot
clip_heist_arrival.text: And the plug. Hairdryer. Pull it near the book.

clip_heist_arrival.speaker: patch
clip_heist_arrival.text: You're very mysterious for a full stop.

spine_arrival.speaker: patch
spine_arrival.text: Okay. That's a lot of up.

spine_arrival.speaker: corrugate
spine_arrival.text: Bindwell's pitons are in. Good, solid work. You zip, I'll... be lifted, somehow, with dignity.

spine_lowpoint.speaker: narrator
spine_lowpoint.text: Near the top, a shelf of wet snow broke loose above Patch. Corrugate shoved him clear, and took all of it.

spine_lowpoint.speaker: corrugate
spine_lowpoint.text: ...Soaked through. Both sides. It's fine. It's fine, fox. Give me a minute by the fire.

spine_lowpoint.speaker: patch
spine_lowpoint.text: You didn't have to do that. That was... why would you do that?

spine_lowpoint.speaker: corrugate
spine_lowpoint.text: Because you'd have done it for me. You're a liar, fox, but you're not a coward.

spine_lowpoint.speaker: patch
spine_lowpoint.text: No. Listen. I didn't lose my tail to a thunderstorm. Or a dragon. Or a bet with the moon.

spine_lowpoint.speaker: patch
spine_lowpoint.text: When the water came onto the title page, I ran. I didn't help anybody. I just ran, and the page tore, and I left part of me back there in the flood.

spine_lowpoint.speaker: patch
spine_lowpoint.text: And ever since, I keep thinking... what if that's it? What if I'm just broken now, and everyone can see it, and all the stories are just me trying to make the tear look cool.

spine_lowpoint.speaker: corrugate
spine_lowpoint.text: Fox. Look at me. I'm a box. I've been wet four times. I've got tape on my tape. My left side's never been straight since a cat sat on it.

spine_lowpoint.speaker: patch
spine_lowpoint.text: ...Did you just make a punctuation joke at my lowest moment?

spine_lowpoint.speaker: patch
spine_lowpoint.text: ...Thanks. Really. Okay. Okay. Let's go and stop the Sogg. Properly, this time. No stories.

sogg_arrival.speaker: sogg
sogg_arrival.text: Little fox. You ran from me once.

sogg_arrival.speaker: patch
sogg_arrival.text: Yeah. I did. I'm not running now.

sogg_arrival.speaker: sogg
sogg_arrival.text: Everything gets wet eventually. Everything sags. Why keep standing up?

sogg_arrival.speaker: patch
sogg_arrival.text: Because someone keeps standing us up. Every night. With a hairdryer and an iron and way too much tape.

sogg_arrival.speaker: dot
sogg_arrival.text: Fold marks. Down there. Slam them.

sogg_drags_patch.speaker: sogg
sogg_drags_patch.text: Enough. ENOUGH. If I can't stop the rain, then nobody stays dry.

sogg_drags_patch.speaker: sogg
sogg_drags_patch.text: Come down, little fox. Down to the Gutter, where it's quiet and nothing has to be fixed.

sogg_drags_patch.speaker: narrator
sogg_drags_patch.text: The Sogg tore through the spine's last stitches and dragged Patch down into the Gutter, the drowned crease at the very middle of the book.
